subject: Post-call: CloudFin integration & SDK next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@cloudfin.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@cloudfin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: CloudFin integration & SDK next steps

Hi Jordan + Priya,

Thanks again for the productive call today — appreciate you walking through the search/ranking workflow and the specific pain points. Quick recap to make sure we’re aligned and to capture next steps: 

Pain points we heard
- High tail latency on model-backed reranking during peak trading hours (spikes to ~1.8s/token)
- Cost unpredictability as query volume scales (embeddings + rerank per query)
- Need for deterministic, structured outputs for downstream compliance tooling

Goals
- Reduce end-to-end rerank latency by ~40% and stabilize tail latency
- Lower per-query cost by batching/caching and targeted quantization profiles
- Deliver structured, strongly-typed rank outputs to integrate with your audit pipeline

Integration / product fit notes
- SDK: you’ll want the streaming responses + function calling path for live rerank pipelines. Our SDK (node/python) supports incremental streaming of candidate scores and structured JSON outputs for immediate consumption.
- Embeddings + reranking: recommend embedding + approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) on your side for candidate retrieval, then Redwood for reranking with structured score outputs and optional provenance tokens.
- Structured outputs: we can map model responses to a strict JSON schema using our function-calling layer to ensure your compliance checks receive consistent fields (score, reason_code, policy_flags).
- Performance levers: enable prefix KV caching for repeated context, and Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching) for the reranker model.

Proposed next steps
1) Tech POC: grant us a short-term test dataset and a staging endpoint. We’ll run a 2-week POC focusing on latency and cost metrics (Mar 9–20).
2) SOW draft: attached a high-level proposal + scope. Please review and flag anything missing.
3) Follow-up: 30-min sync to walk through the POC plan and acceptance criteria — propose Thu Mar 11 at 10:00am PT.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); cloudfin-postcall-notes.docx (DOCX, internal notes)

If this looks right, I’ll queue the POC environment and send calendar invites.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@cloudfin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@cloudfin.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: CloudFin integration & SDK next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the discussion well. A couple quick clarifications/questions from our side: 

- POC dataset: we can share a redacted week of traffic (about 200k queries) by end of day Fri. Will that be sufficient for an initial latency/cost assessment?
- Streaming + function calling: important that we get intermediate scores for each candidate rather than waiting for a final aggregated response. Your note sounds like that’s supported — any sample payloads you can share?
- Compliance: for structured outputs, we need a schema that includes a stable reason_code and a confidence field (0.0–1.0). Can you confirm Redwood’s function response mapping can enforce types and required fields?

We’re aligned on the Mar 11 sync — 10am PT works for Priya and me.

Appreciate the fast turnaround on the SOW.

—Jordan
Jordan Hayes
Head of Search Infrastructure, CloudFin
j.hayes@cloudfin.com

Thanks Jordan — great questions. Quick answers inline: 

- POC dataset: 200k queries is perfect for an initial run. We’ll sample and synthetic-augment if we need more long-tail cases.
- Streaming/payloads: attaching a short example payload for the streaming function-calling flow (see attachment: streaming-example.json stub in the proposal PDF). The streaming path emits per-candidate score events and a final aggregate.
- Schema enforcement: yes — our function-calling wrapper will validate fields and types against a provided JSON schema. We can include reason_code (string enum) and confidence (float 0.0–1.0) as required fields in the POC contract.

Next steps (I’ll action these today):
- Stand up a staging endpoint and share creds by EOD Fri (Mar 6).
- Load the redacted dataset when you share it; we'll run the initial latency baseline and return metrics within 3 business days of ingest.
- Send calendar invite for Mar 11 10:00am PT and include an agenda: POC scope, acceptance criteria, and success metrics.

If anything changes on your side, let me know — otherwise we’ll proceed as above.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: CloudFin POC scope and ask

Rishi / Logan — quick internal note following the CloudFin call and the external thread. Key asks for the eng/solutions side: 

1) Can we prep a staging endpoint with the reranker model (quantized FP16) and streaming+function-calling enabled? Target: credentials to customer by EOD Fri (Mar 6).
2) Logan: please draft the JSON schema for the structured output (fields: candidate_id, score, reason_code, confidence, provenance_token). I’ll review and send to CloudFin to lock for the POC.
3) Rishi: plan to run an initial latency baseline once the redacted dataset lands — we should instrument tail latency (p95/p99) and per-token cost. Aim to return first metrics within 3 business days after ingest.

I’ve attached the proposal and the call notes to the external thread for context. I’ll coordinate calendar invites.

Thanks —
